In detail

Hägersten-Älvsjö is one of Stockholm's 11 official stadsdelsnamnder (city district committees). Bra (Brottsforebyggande radet), Sweden's national crime-prevention council, recorded 19,805 total reported offences here in 2025, across a population of 128,794 residents (Stockholms stad, 31 December 2024) — a rate of 15,377 offences per 100,000 residents, close to the citywide average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central, station, or nightlife-heavy district can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential district can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Stockholm — real Bra / Stockholms stad figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Hägersten-Älvsjö safe?

Wandroz currently rates Hägersten-Älvsjö in Stockholm, Sweden as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Stockholm, Sweden, based on Brå (Brottsförebyggande rådet)'s 2025 reported-offence data. This source has no time-of-day breakdown, so this is one overall level rather than a separately measured day and night figure — see the note on this page before treating the day/night badges as independently measured.

Does Hägersten-Älvsjö's rating cover night-time safety specifically?

Not separately. Brå (Brottsförebyggande rådet)'s 2025 reported-offence data publishes one figure per zone with no time-of-day split, so Hägersten-Älvsjö's day and night badges show the same underlying level rather than an independently measured night figure. Treat it as a general indicator, not a night-specific measurement.

Is Hägersten-Älvsjö a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Hägersten-Älvsjö's rating is a useful general indicator, but this data is normalised against registered residents, not visitor footfall — busy tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher without that meaning elevated risk for a visitor passing through.
